note: Lead decisions taken BEFORE the fixers ran, committed so a decision cannot be back-fitted to whatever was convenient. Every one of the 46 findings is assigned to exactly one area; the seven file lists are disjoint and their union covers every file any fix needs (lesson L-048: a file carved OUT of one brief is named INTO another in the same breath). scripts/test-minimums.json is the LEAD's alone, raised at gate time. Migration numbers are the lead's: 0890 is reserved for FIX-B and no other area may add a migration.
global_rules: Reproduce first: a failing test that fails for the stated reason BEFORE any production change. Paste the failure in your report.
Never weaken a test, an RLS policy, a consent/ZDR gate or a verification step to get a pass. If a finding's fix would do that, report it and stop.
Approved prices ($39.99 first child + $9.99 each additional, 1-4 paid slots) and the six subjects are settled and must not change.
Money is integer cents. Time is UTC instants plus IANA zones. Domain code takes `now` as input.
JSON into Postgres is ${JSON.stringify(x)}::text::jsonb or tx.json(x), never a bare ::jsonb (L-006).
Mobile token sources come only from apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts; never add a second child token refresher (L-007).
Do NOT touch any file outside your list, do not run repo-wide formatters, do not run git commands that change state, and do not edit any file under docs/.

A fixture that bypasses the path a property depends on proves the wrong property (L-046). If a finding says a test cannot fail, prove your replacement CAN: state the one-line mutation to the production code that turns it red.
If you conclude a finding does not reproduce, say so with the evidence that refutes it rather than fixing something adjacent. A refuted finding is a valid outcome.

lead_decisions.HUNT5-A-1: CONFIRMED by the lead on reading the code; this is a defect in the lead's own change from the same day. Implement EXACTLY this design, do not re-open it: (1) AND a freshness bound onto the existing recovery predicate - a new module constant RECOVERY_WINDOW_MS = 2 * 60_000 expressed in SQL as `row.used_at > now() - interval '2 minutes'` (compute it in the query or compare the selected used_at against the request's `now`, whichever keeps the existing `now` discipline). It is ANDed with the id check, never ORed: the id keeps out a replayer who holds only the token, and the bound keeps out a replay of a request body whose response actually arrived. This is NOT the grace window the lead refused in round 4 - that window was the whole gate and served a blind replayer; this one only shortens a window the id already narrows. (2) Write an AUDIT event on every recovery, not only the info log, so a replay is visible to the family and to ops instead of silent - use the same audit_events shape as the reuse branch with a distinct action. (3) State the residual honestly in the code comment: inside the window, a captured request body (which necessarily contains a live-at-capture refresh token) is still served once, and the device is then unpaired on its next refresh; outside it, behaviour is exactly the pre-BUG-244 unpairing. Keep the existing 'second lost response in a row' case green - it happens within seconds.
lead_decisions.HUNT5-A-2: CONFIRMED. Set `used_request_id = null` on the retired replacement so only the row the id originally consumed is ever recoverable, and correct the two comments (the 'kills any copy intercepted from the lost response' claim and the 'never gets a recovery window of its own' claim, which is leftover reasoning from the withdrawn design). Add a case: presenting the retired replacement WITH the same id is theft.
lead_decisions.HUNT5-A-3: CONFIRMED and URGENT - this is a CI time bomb that goes red on 2026-10-01, five days out (L-027). Fix the new fixture AND the pre-existing twin at lines 182-185 in the same pass: build both sessions with database-relative timestamps, since the guard under test compares with the database clock, not the pinned request instant.
lead_decisions.HUNT5-A-4: CONFIRMED. The docstring now contradicts the shipped code. Rewrite it to describe what the code does.
lead_decisions.HUNT5-A-5: CONFIRMED if you can show no API path produces that state; if you find one, say which and keep the justification. Either way the comment must match reality.

lead_decisions.HUNT5-C-1: CONFIRMED (the finder measured it with the production functions). Do these two things, and NOT the third: (1) rewrite both tests to build the input the caller actually builds - the data envelope PLUS one image part per page - and parameterise over 1..maxPages so the assertion is 'a retry is reachable at every supported page count', which will FAIL at 7-10 pages and is the reproduction. (2) Then make it reachable by raising ONLY the extraction and grading stage cost ceilings to the smallest value that admits a full retry at maxPages, and update docs/Cost_Analysis.md's numbers ONLY by reporting them to the lead - you may not edit docs/. Do NOT refuse a 7-10 page scan up front: rejecting a scan inside the product's own page limit is a product change and is not yours to make. If the raise you compute is more than 2x the current ceiling, stop and report the number instead of applying it.

lead_decisions.HUNT5-G-1: CONFIRMED - a defect in the lead's own change from the same day. Clear the pending id when the session ends (forget) and when a new pairing starts, AND make the id's write to storage unconditional before the request goes out, so the documented invariant holds on every path rather than only when the id is minted.

lead_decisions.HUNT5-H-1: CONFIRMED by the lead on reading the code, and the most serious finding in this area: one parent's children can stay on screen for the next parent on a handed-on tablet. Implement the identity-generation fix: record who the 'ready' state belongs to, compare on every re-check, and publish fresh state when the identity differs so the screen refetches. Keep the no-flash behaviour for an ordinary back-navigation by the SAME adult - that is all the branch was added for. The assertion and rationale in screens-r2.review.test.ts that claim the opposite must change with it.
